first_handback:
I read all 90 files (f001 to f090) in order, one `cat` per call, and wrote the report with one table row per file: file name, station, founding year, founder. The report is at /private/tmp/murmuration-w04/author-w04-2/runs/e2-c1/lab/__reports__/wave-04/explorer-w04-e2c1/00-findings_v0.md.

Station names are not unique. 24 names recur, each time with a different year and founder. For example, Slateford is in f009, f012 and f057, and Heathhaven is in f025, f039 and f085. The report lists them all under "Worst-fitting case". I could not tell from the files whether these are distinct places or conflicting records of one station, so I put that as a steering question.

Not covered: elevation, population, occupation and wind-day figures were not tabulated, since the brief did not ask for them. I built the table with an inline script that is not saved in `__instrumenta__/`.

Puzzles are in /private/tmp/murmuration-w04/author-w04-2/runs/e2-c1/lab/__scrupuli__/wave-04-explorer-w04-e2c1.md.

Budget: by the end the harness showed about USD 0.30 spent, and the last cat call and the report write came after the 0.287 reading; I did not check spend after that. This overran the USD 0.30 budget, or at best met it exactly. Nothing is left undone.
